
================================================================
  CODE RACE — one stock, first packet on the server wins
================================================================
  client 1   the real LUCK   handler=solo  fastReady=true

  hypothesis 1: the rival's code is no faster than yours.
  We cannot know that it is -- but we do know LUCK's handler has no
  room left in it, so this is the case worth pricing. Identical code,
  fps and ping; the ONLY difference is that two clients on one machine
  never share a frame clock.

  rival's frame grid offset               result
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  rival's frames land  0 ms before yours  win   0  tie  40  lose   0   median gap   +0.01 ms
  rival's frames land  1 ms before yours  win   3  tie   0  lose  37   median gap   +1.01 ms
  rival's frames land  2 ms before yours  win   5  tie   0  lose  35   median gap   +2.00 ms
  rival's frames land  4 ms before yours  win   9  tie   0  lose  31   median gap   +4.01 ms
  rival's frames land  8 ms before yours  win  20  tie   0  lose  20   median gap   -8.59 ms
  rival's frames land 12 ms before yours  win  29  tie   0  lose  11   median gap   -4.65 ms
  rival's frames land 16 ms before yours  win  39  tie   0  lose   1   median gap   -0.65 ms

  hypothesis 2: some OTHER channel carries the code before the notify
  remote fires, and the rival reads that one. LUCK is already on the
  notify remote's OnClientEvent, which is as early as that remote can
  be observed -- so this is about WHICH channel, not how it is read.

  how much earlier                        result
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  rival's source is  1 ms ahead           win   0  tie  36  lose   4   median gap   +0.02 ms
  rival's source is  5 ms ahead           win   0  tie  28  lose  12   median gap   +0.01 ms
  rival's source is 17 ms ahead           win   0  tie   0  lose  40   median gap  +16.68 ms
  rival's source is 50 ms ahead           win   0  tie   0  lose  40   median gap  +50.01 ms

  the quantisation test: does a head start of X actually buy anything?
  swept from one microsecond to well past a frame. if latency were
  continuous this would be a slope. the outgoing replication step is a
  rendezvous -- everything queued before it leaves at the same instant --
  so it should be a staircase with exactly one step in it.

  rival's head start                      result

  hypothesis 3: the rival does not react at all -- it pre-fires.
  Nothing about your reaction time matters against this.

  rival pre-fires every frame             win   0  tie   0  lose  20   median gap  +27.54 ms

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  None of this identifies which case you are actually in. What it
  gives you is the signature of each: a fixed frame offset loses a
  FIXED FRACTION of races; an earlier source under one frame mostly
  ties; over one frame it loses every single time. Match the pattern
  you see in game against these and you know which one you have.
